notes: Complete leaf owner: loads the shared buffer pointer Data_03001ed0, then writes one 12-byte DMA3 descriptor (source, destination, control) to 0x040000d4 and returns. No calls, branches, or loops.

The reference emits the descriptor with a single `stmia r3!, {r0, r1, r2}` (registers built directly, no stack) followed by a dead `subs r3, #12`. Every ordinary-C spelling of the same three field writes -- direct field assignment through a volatile struct macro, the identical assignment through a non-volatile struct macro, and the historically adopted raw `u32 *p; p[0..2] = ...` form -- compiles under the approved GCC 2.96 route to three separate `str` instructions instead, never the multi-register transfer. The tool's own scorer classifies every one of these candidates `unemittable`.

This is the same DMA3-descriptor-via-struct-macro idiom already established unemittable in this overlay at resource_392:02000bcc (see resource_392_c_02000bcc.json) and recorded across the wider thumb_multi_register_module family in games/gs1/semantic/overlay-assembly.json (not yet including this address's own span). No new compiler evidence needed to be produced; this owner reconfirms the existing conclusion for a smaller, single-transfer case.

games/gs1/semantic/regions.json records this exact 32-byte span as `parked by overlay park`: an earlier adopted C candidate (raw u32 pointer-array form, recovered from git history at assets/code/resource_392_c_02000b8c.c, commit d5e9214a5) stopped reproducing the span after an infrastructure change ('the pret routing cut') and was reverted to assembly.
